text.p: - Menatep, one of the biggest private banks, is striving to establish control over the strategically important fertiliser branch of industry of Russia's economy.
- A number of civilian casualties in Chechnya might exceed 80,000 -- the figure annonced by security chief Alexander Lebed.
- The communists insist that peace agreements on Chechnya are invalid and are calling on parliament to intervene.
- After the second missile strike at Iraq the UN Security Council is deciding whether United States is right or not.
- The bombing of Iraq has caused a temporary rise in oil prices, boosting Russia's export activity.
- Russia's Central Bank chief promised to knock zeros off the Russian rouble only after it has stabilised.
- A second missile attack on Iraq proves that the United States had not expected any permission for a military action.
- Political speculation around peace deals on Chechnya continue, but people are being still killed in the region.
- The fight for control over the aluminium industry seems to have ended - the biggest section has been won by Trans World Group.

- "Is is good that Bill is Boris's close friend otherwise we would have been punished for disobedience," says the paper referring to the United States missile raids to tame Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein.
- Tension around Iraq is threatening to cause the most serious crisis in Russian-American relations in recent years.
- A senior Moscow police official will face court charges for extorting $400 from a local businessman.
